login.title: Sign in
login.text: Sign in with Telegram or with your email. The way in changes nothing: same account, same cards, same history.
login.key: Sign in with an access key
login.webapp.title: Sign in with Telegram
login.webapp.text: The app is open from Telegram, so no separate sign-in is needed: your account is linked to this Telegram account.
login.email.title: Sign in with email
login.email.text: The confirmation code goes to this address, and so does account recovery.
login.password.title: Create a password
login.password.text: The password is for signing in from the web and from a computer, where there is no Telegram.
login.confirm.title: Confirm your email
login.confirm.resend: No email? Check the spam folder or request a new code.
onboarding.link.title: Get started
onboarding.link.text: This is a corporate card platform. To begin, enter the code your administrator gave you.
onboarding.link.invalid: That code did not work. Check that you entered all of it, or ask your administrator for a new one.
onboarding.link.throttled: Too many attempts. Try again in {minutes} minutes.
onboarding.pin.title: App PIN
onboarding.pin.text: Choose a PIN. You will need it to view card details and confirm important actions. This is not the PIN of the card itself.
onboarding.recovery.title: Recovery code
onboarding.recovery.text: Save this code. It lets you sign in from a different Telegram account if you lose access to this one. We cannot recover it for you.
profile.pending.title: Profile under review
profile.pending.text: Your profile is being reviewed. This usually takes from a few hours to a couple of days. You will be able to issue a card once the review is done — we will notify you.
profile.stuck.title: Review paused
profile.stuck.text: The profile review has been paused. We are looking into it and an administrator will contact you.
profile.blocked.title: Access closed
profile.blocked.text: Access is closed. Contact your administrator.
profile.quarantine.title: Restricted after Telegram change
profile.quarantine.text: For security reasons some actions are unavailable until {until}. If this was not you, contact your administrator immediately.
home.empty.title: Top up your balance to issue a card.
home.hasBalance.text: You have {amount} in your account. Issue a card to start spending.
card.frozen.byUser.text: The card is frozen. Payments will not go through.
card.frozen.negative.text: The card is frozen: your account is {amount} short. Top up your balance and the card will unlock automatically.
card.unfreeze.confirm.title: Unfreeze the card?
card.unfreeze.confirm.text: Payments on this card will start going through again.
card.canceled.text: The card is closed. Its activity is available in your history.
card.limit.title: Maximum reached
card.limit.text: You can have no more than two cards. To issue a new one, close one of the current cards.
issue.title: Issue a card
issue.first.text: This will be your primary card. Your whole balance moves to it automatically.
issue.second.text: A second card is funded by transfer from the primary one. You can set the amount now or transfer later.
issue.slow: This is taking longer than usual, the card will appear on its own
issue.failed.title: Did not work
issue.failed.text: We could not issue the card. Your money is untouched, please try again.
transfer.title: Transfer between cards
transfer.confirm.title: Transfer {amount}?
transfer.stuck.title: Transfer in progress
transfer.stuck.text: This transfer is taking longer than usual. Your money is safe, we will finish the operation automatically.
transfer.blocked: Wait for the previous transfer to finish
negative.title: Negative balance
negative.text: A charge went over your available amount — this happens with hotels, tips or exchange rate changes. Your cards are frozen for now. Top up {amount} and they will work again.
topup.title: Top up
topup.network.text: {asset}. Choose the network you will send it over.
topup.min.warning: Below the minimum. We will accept the request, the operator decides.
topup.address.title: Deposit address
topup.address.warning: Send only on the {network} network and only {asset}. Sending on another network means losing the money.
topup.address.heading: {asset} · {network}
topup.address.only: Send only {asset} over the {network} network. Other coins may be lost.
topup.address.ownText: The address belongs to you and deposits on it are credited automatically. Do not pass it on: someone else’s transfer would be credited to you and go through the same screening.
topup.create.title: No address yet
topup.create.subtitle: {asset} · {network}
topup.create.text: The address is created for you personally and stays yours: when money lands on it the system knows the transfer is yours and credits it without waiting for an operator.
topup.create.burnedTitle: The old address no longer works
topup.create.burnedText: It was burned after money that failed screening was sent back. Do not send anything to it — create a new one.
topup.address.memoWarning: Without the memo the transfer will not be credited.
topup.calc.title: What gets credited
topup.calc.subtitle: The amount is yours to choose. Use the preset amounts to see what reaches the account.
topup.form.title: Confirm your transfer
topup.form.linkHint: Without a link the request may be rejected
topup.pending.title: Request under review
topup.pending.text: Request received. Review usually takes up to {hours} hours during working hours. We will notify you.
topup.rejected.title: Request rejected
secrets.title: Card details
secrets.throttled.title: Too many requests
secrets.throttled.text: Too many requests. Try again in {minutes} minutes.
pin.title: Card PIN
pin.text: This PIN is used when paying with the card. It is not the same as your app PIN.
close.title: Closing a card
close.step1.title: Close card {last4}?
close.step1.text: The card will be blocked and new payments will not go through. This is reversible until the card is finally closed.
close.step1.warning: There is no reissue: a new card gets a different number, and subscriptions and saved payments will stop working.
close.step1.confirm: Enter the last 4 digits of the card
close.step2.title: Where the remaining money goes
close.step2.child: The remaining money returns to your primary card automatically.
close.step2.toChild: Move to card {last4} — it becomes the primary one
close.step2.toNew: Issue a new card and move the money to it
close.step2.noChild: There is no secondary card. The remaining money moves to a newly issued card.
close.step3.title: Waiting for unfinished payments
close.step3.text: The card is closing. {amount} is held by {count} unfinished payments. The money is released automatically, usually within a few days. After that the card closes.
close.step3.return: Put the card back in service
close.step4.title: Card closed
close.step4.text: The card is closed. Its activity is available in your history.
close.failed.title: Could not issue the new card
close.failed.text: We could not issue the new card. The current one is still active and your money is untouched. Please try again.
history.title: Activity
history.empty.title: No activity yet
history.empty.text: Payments and top-ups will appear here once you start using the card.
op.detail.title: Transaction
op.detail.rateNote: The rate is derived: we divide the charged amount by the merchant amount. No official rate comes with the transaction.
op.detail.diff.rate: The exchange rate changed since the payment.
op.detail.diff.tips: The merchant added to the amount — a tip or extra services.
op.detail.refund.note: The merchant refunded the full amount; the difference comes from the exchange rate changing.
pool.title: Maintenance
pool.text: Maintenance is under way, payments are temporarily unavailable.
offline.title: Service temporarily unavailable
offline.text: The service is temporarily unavailable. Data may be updated with a delay.
challenge.title: Confirmation code
challenge.expired.title: Code expired
challenge.expired.text: The code for the {amount} · {merchant} purchase is no longer valid. Repeat the payment to get a new one.
notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.empty.title: No notifications yet
notifications.empty.text: Payments, deposits and payment confirmation codes will show up here.
notify.challenge.code.title: Payment confirmation code
notify.challenge.code.text: {merchant} — {amount} {currency}. Never share this code with anyone.
notify.spend.completed.title: Payment
notify.spend.declined.title: Payment declined
notify.deposit.credited.title: Deposit confirmed
notify.deposit.rejected.title: Deposit request rejected
notify.transfer.completed.title: Transfer complete
notify.card.issued.title: Card issued
notify.card.issued.text: Card ••{last4} is ready to pay with.
notify.card.frozen.title: Card frozen
notify.card.frozen.text: Card ••{last4} is frozen, payments with it are stopped.
notify.aml.failed.title: A deposit failed screening
notify.aml.failed.text: {amount} {currency} arrived on your address but was not credited. You can send it back to the sender.
incoming.title: Active transactions
incoming.subtitle: Deposits we can see right now
incoming.rejectedText: The money is safe and sits on your address. We cannot credit it — it can be sent back to the sender.
refund.title: Refund
refund.offer.title: Send the money back
refund.offer.text: {amount} arrived on your address on {network}, but it did not pass origin screening and was not credited.
refund.why.title: The money is safe
refund.why.text: It sits on your deposit address. We cannot credit it, but we can send it back — to where it came from.
refund.calc.title: What comes back
refund.calc.subtitle: The network fee is withheld by the service that sends the transfer. We take no fee: nothing was credited.
refund.toHint: The same one the money came from. No other address can be entered.
refund.afterHint: After sending, this deposit address stops working.
refund.sent.title: Refund sent
refund.sent.text: The money went back to the sender address. It usually takes a few minutes.
refund.burned.title: The deposit address was burned
refund.burned.text: This address no longer works: it is tied to a transfer that failed screening. Create a new one for your next deposit.
settings.title: Settings
settings.email.text: Confirmation and account recovery go to this address.
settings.email.confirmText: We will send a code to the new address. Until the code is entered the email counts as unconfirmed and the old one keeps working.
settings.password.text: Needed for signing in from the web and from a computer, outside Telegram.
settings.twofa.text: Second factor for signing in with email: an authenticator app or a code by email.
settings.twofa.support: Turning the second factor off is only possible through support.
settings.twofa.app.text: Scan the code in Google Authenticator or another one-time password app, then enter the six-digit code it shows.
settings.twofa.email.text: We sent a code to {email}. Enter it to connect the second factor.
recovery.title: Recover access
recovery.text: Enter the recovery code you saved when you first connected.
recovery.done.title: Access recovered
recovery.done.text: Set a new app PIN. Your previous recovery code no longer works — we have issued a new one.
recovery.quarantine: For 24 hours, viewing card details, changing the card PIN and withdrawals will be unavailable.
admin.shell.search: Search by name, last4 or merchant
admin.shell.signOutText: The session will end, and getting back in needs the password and the code from your authenticator. Any open dialogs with unsaved edits will be lost.
admin.login.subtitle: Admin. Operators only.
admin.login.codeHint: Six digits from your authenticator app.
admin.login.lostText: Another operator resets it from the Operators section. There is no self-service recovery: access to the admin is access to other people’s money.
admin.login.proto: Prototype: nothing is verified, any values will do. What you type is not sent anywhere.
admin.profile.title: Profile
admin.profile.languageHint: Only our own wording changes. Data from the issuer arrives in English and is not translated.
admin.profile.scanHint: Scan it with your authenticator app or enter the key by hand. The key is shown once.
admin.profile.enabledText: Sign-in asks for a code every time. To move it to another device, set it up again — the old one stops working.
admin.profile.warnTitle: Admin access without a second factor
admin.profile.warnText: A password alone is not enough: deposits are approved and balances are adjusted from here. Set up a second factor.
admin.profile.mismatch: Does not match the new password
admin.dashboard.title: Dashboard
admin.dashboard.note: What needs attention comes first. The pool is our working capital pledged with the issuer, not a store of users’ money: their crypto arrives at separate wallets. Coverage shows whether the working capital is sufficient.
admin.revenue.profitHint: What we withheld on deposits and withdrawals. Company and user money is not part of this.
admin.coverage.ok.label: Normal
admin.coverage.ok.hint: Headroom is sufficient. Nothing to do.
admin.coverage.warn20.label: 20% threshold
admin.coverage.warn20.hint: First warning. Plan a top-up of the pool.
admin.coverage.warn15.label: 15% threshold
admin.coverage.warn15.hint: Headroom is shrinking. Top the pool up within days.
admin.coverage.urgent10.label: 10% threshold
admin.coverage.urgent10.hint: Top up this company’s pool now.
admin.coverage.critical.label: Critical
admin.coverage.critical.hint: Cards may already be declining: the issuer checks the pool before the card limit, so declines land at random.
admin.dashboard.queue.title: Needs action
admin.dashboard.queue.subtitle: Each row opens its section with the filter applied
admin.dashboard.queue.stuckMeta: Only their account manager can resolve these
admin.dashboard.queue.closingMeta: Waiting for open authorizations to settle
admin.dashboard.queue.errorsMeta: With a requestId for issuer support
admin.dashboard.catchUpHint: The GET /events catch-up is mandatory: webhooks are delivered once, with no retries. If the endpoint was down, the event is lost for good — only the catch-up recovers it.
admin.col.name: Name
admin.users.title: Users
admin.users.note: There is no deletion in this system: an account can only be blocked, and that is reversible. The ledger, the operation history and the audit log are financial records, and a cardholder cannot be erased at Oxen.
admin.users.emptyText: Try a different status, clear the search, or drop the company filter.
admin.cards.title: Cards
admin.cards.note: Editing a limit directly is not provided: the limit is derived from the allocation the user makes. Nor is there a direct cancel that skips closing — cancellation at Oxen is irreversible.
admin.cards.emptyText: Try a different status or type, or drop the company filter.
admin.deposits.title: Deposits
admin.deposits.note: A request is created by the user after they have already sent the funds. Confirming the arrival happens outside the system, by hand. Oldest requests first.
admin.deposits.historyNote: History of crediting. The system credits on its own; everything lands here — credited, held by screening, and whatever an operator entered by hand.
admin.deposits.manualText: Automatic crediting is off: every deposit waits for an operator. The switch is under "Fees".
admin.deposits.emptyText: Try a different status or drop the company filter.
admin.tx.title: Transactions
admin.tx.note: The merchant name arrives raw from the issuer and is shown as is: their API has no logos or categories. Anomalies are marked with a bar on the left.
admin.tx.emptyText: Try a different status, clear the search, or drop the company filter.
admin.audit.title: Audit log
admin.audit.note: Every operator action that moves money is written here with the amount, the user and the reason. Entries cannot be deleted.
admin.audit.toastText: The ledger, the operation history and this log are financial records. That is why the product has neither a delete-user button nor a delete-entry one.
admin.audit.emptyText: Try a different operator or action type.
admin.system.title: System status
admin.system.note: A discrepancy noticed a month later can no longer be reconstructed. That is why reconciliation runs on a schedule, not on demand.
admin.system.lagHint: Webhooks are delivered once, with no retries. If the endpoint was down, the event is lost for good — only the catch-up recovers it.
admin.system.unprocessedHint: An event is a notification, not a record. Handling it re-reads the resource and applies the change in a single transaction.
admin.system.lastPoolReadHint: Pool reads share one rate limit, so we poll them rarely.
admin.system.throttlingHint: Exceeding the shared rate limit returns a 401 indistinguishable from a bad key. Retrying it in a loop makes things worse.
admin.system.transfersSubtitle: Need attention: the second issuer call is not confirmed yet
admin.system.transfersHint: The order is mandatory: the source limit is reduced first, the destination limit raised second. So a failure of the second call means funds temporarily out of reach, not money from thin air. A background process finishes the transfer.
admin.system.stuckHint: Card issuance must not be retried: a second request issues a second card. Re-read the resource instead of repeating the call.
admin.system.errorsHint: The requestId is what issuer support needs. Only codes on the allow-list may be retried: they have no «5xx is retryable» rule.
admin.system.keysHint: Access keys for these services live in environment variables and are never shown in the admin panel.
admin.service.note.amlUnavailable: Checks are not going through — automatic crediting stopped
admin.system.sourceTitle: Our database is the only source of truth for balances
admin.system.sourceText: The issuer does not keep our balances and cannot restore them. Hence the requirement for backups and a rehearsed restore procedure.
admin.recon.ledgerMirror.title: Ledger against the transaction mirror
admin.recon.balancesPools.title: Balances against pools
admin.exchange.title: Exchange log
admin.exchange.note: What went to the issuer and what came back. The requestId is what their support needs: they have their log, we have ours, and this number ties them together.
admin.exchange.secretsText: Card number, CVV, PIN and access keys are stripped before the entry is written, not when it is displayed. Card details are decrypted on the user’s device and never reach our server.
admin.exchange.emptyText: Try a different direction or outcome, or clear the search.
admin.exchange.sentHint: The idempotency key is written to the database BEFORE sending: otherwise, if the process dies, we will not know whether the card was issued and will issue a second one.
admin.exchange.receivedHint: The card number and CVV are masked in the stored entry, not just on screen: in the clear they never reach our server.
admin.exchange.note.409: The limit changed concurrently. We re-read the card and applied the change again — the request itself must not be repeated.
admin.exchange.note.401: Indistinguishable from exceeding the shared rate limit. We do not retry in a loop: it would make things worse.
admin.exchange.note.502: The code is not on the allow-list. A retry would issue a second card, so we re-read the card list instead.
admin.exchange.note.amlFailed: Risk score above the threshold. The deposit was held and nothing was credited.
admin.exchange.note.amlUnavailable: The screening service did not answer. Unchecked money is not credited, so the deposit went into the queue.
admin.exchange.note.refundSent: Refund to the sender of a deposit that failed screening.
admin.fees.title: Fees
admin.fees.note: The rate is frozen into the entry at the moment it applies. Changing the global rate does not recompute past operations and takes effect going forward only.
admin.fees.autoSubtitle: Who credits the money: the system, when it lands on an issued address, or an operator by hand.
admin.fees.autoHint: Switching this off restores the old order: a deposit goes into the queue and waits for an operator. The queue stays either way — everything the system could not credit lands in it.
admin.fees.amlMaxRiskHint: Above this score a deposit is not credited but held for a decision. The scale belongs to the external screening service; we have none of our own.
admin.fees.confirmationsHint: How many confirmations we wait for before treating the money as arrived.
admin.fees.withoutAmlSwitch: Credit even when screening does not answer
admin.fees.withoutAmlHint: Off: while screening is unavailable deposits wait for an operator. Turning it on means that during an outage at a third-party service money is credited with no origin screening at all.
admin.fees.amlDownPassing: Deposits are being credited without origin screening — that is how this is configured. While the service is silent, everything gets through.
admin.fees.amlDownText: While the screening service is silent automatic crediting does not work: unchecked deposits pile up in the queue instead of being credited on trust. Service status is under "System state".
admin.fees.readOnlyText: Changing this needs the MANAGE_SETTINGS right.
admin.fees.savedText: The new values apply to operations from this moment on. Past entries keep the rate they were made at.
admin.fees.unsavedText: Until Save is pressed, the rates stay as they were.
admin.fees.minDepositHint: A warning, not a block: if a smaller amount has already been sent, the operator approves it with a reason.
admin.fees.calcSubtitle: Enter an amount and see the result for both rates
admin.fees.calcHint: In the prototype this is a worked example: the actual arithmetic arrives in stage 1, with tests.
admin.fees.overridesSubtitle: A per-user rate REPLACES the global one, it is not added to it
admin.fees.confirmHint: Past operations are not recomputed: every entry keeps the rate it was made at. The change takes effect going forward and lands in the audit log.
admin.txDrawer.title: Operation
admin.txDrawer.poolHint: A decline on the company pool, not on the card. The user sees it as «technical maintenance»: the state of the pool is none of their business and nothing they can affect. The admin shows the real reason.
admin.txDrawer.lookRequestId: requestId — that is what issuer support needs.
admin.txDrawer.lookLocal: The merchant amount is stored for display only and takes no part in arithmetic: the ledger is kept in USD by the settled amount.
admin.txDrawer.lookRate: Their API has no exchange rate and no conversion fee. If we show a rate, it is a derived one, labelled as derived.
admin.txDrawer.anomalyNote: Anomalies feed the reconciliation and the «Needs action» list.
admin.anomalyText.OVER_AUTH: Settled above the authorization. This happens legitimately: an exchange-rate difference or a merchant top-up. Investigate against the authorization amount saved from the event.
admin.anomalyText.FORCE_POSTED: The operation was force-posted, bypassing authorization. Card networks allow this.
admin.anomalyText.NO_AUTH: Settled without an authorization. A hotel, a tip, an offline operation or a late charge.
admin.newUser.pendingText: Usually a few hours to a couple of days. The status arrives as an event — we draw no progress bar, because we do not know which stage the review is at.
admin.newUser.pendingHint: Until the profile is approved, the user can top up their balance but cannot issue a card. They see this explanation in their own app.
admin.newUser.title: New user
admin.newUser.submit: Create and send to the issuer
admin.newUser.lead: These are the fields the issuer requires for a cardholder. The product never says «employee»: cardholders are not necessarily on staff.
admin.newUser.name: Full name
admin.newUser.emailHint: The issuer sends payment confirmation codes there. The rest — phone, date of birth, address — it collects itself during screening.
admin.newUser.step1: A record in our database, together with an idempotency key.
admin.newUser.step2: A call to the issuer to create the cardholder.
admin.newUser.step3: Waiting for the status — it arrives as an event, not as a response.
admin.newUser.step4: A one-time code for linking Telegram.
admin.newUser.keyHint: The key is saved before the request goes out. Repeating the request without it would create a second cardholder, and a cardholder cannot be deleted at Oxen.
admin.cardDrawer.title: Card •••• {last4}
admin.cardDrawer.frozenTitle: Frozen because the balance is negative
admin.cardDrawer.frozenText: It cannot be unfrozen by hand: bring the user’s balance out of the red first, and the card unfreezes on its own.
admin.cardDrawer.closingText: {amount} USD is held by open authorizations. Cancellation happens automatically once the balance is zero and nothing is held. The authorization reserve is not transferred: an operation settling later would push the card and the user into the red.
admin.cardDrawer.ceilingHint: The ceiling does not drop as money is spent — an internal spent counter grows instead. Remaining is the ceiling minus what has been spent.
admin.cardDrawer.needRight: Acting on a card needs the MANAGE_USERS right.
admin.cardDrawer.mismatchHint: We do not hide disagreements with Oxen: if our values diverge from their read, both are shown side by side, with a re-read button next to them.
admin.cardDrawer.closeNotice: The card has been moved to closing. Cancellation happens automatically.
admin.cardDrawer.closeText: The card will be frozen and marked for closing. This is reversible until it is cancelled. Cancellation happens automatically — at a zero balance with no open authorizations.
admin.cardDrawer.remainderTitle: A secondary card’s balance goes to the primary one
admin.cardDrawer.remainderText: For the primary card the choice is made when moving it to closing: transfer to a secondary card that becomes primary, or issue a new one.
admin.companies.title: Companies
admin.companies.note: Each company has its own cl_… at Oxen and its own pool. One company’s pool does not cover another’s cards, so the solvency invariant is computed per company.
admin.companies.readOnlyTitle: The pool deposit address is read-only
admin.companies.readOnlyText: The pool is topped up by hand, from our own funds, outside the platform. We do not withdraw from the collateral through the API either: that goes through the issuer’s administrator.
admin.companies.whyTitle: Why coverage is computed per company
admin.companies.whyText: The issuer checks the company collateral before the card limit. If more limit has been issued than the pool holds, cards start declining at random — whoever spends first gets through. Their API has no such number; we compute it ourselves.
admin.companies.kybTitle: KYB first, the record here second
admin.companies.kybText: We do not create clients through the issuer’s API. A company appears in this list after the check is passed in person and a cl_… is issued.
admin.companies.depositLaterTitle: The deposit address arrives on its own
admin.companies.depositLaterText: The issuer provides it after the company is created. It must not be typed in by hand: a mistake there means the pool goes to someone else’s wallet.
admin.companies.name: Name
admin.companies.kybConfirm: KYB passed, cl_… received from the issuer
admin.companies.oxenIdHint: Change this only if the issuer has issued a new cl_…. Someone else’s identifier sends the cards to someone else’s pool.
admin.companies.depositHintShort: Read-only: the address comes from the issuer.
admin.companies.stateTitle: Pool and coverage are not edited here
admin.companies.stateText: These are not settings but state: the pool is read from the issuer, the coverage is computed by us. They cannot be set by hand — otherwise the screen would show a number unconnected to reality.
admin.networks.title: Networks and coins
admin.networks.note: Which network + coin pairs are open for deposits. The user sees the network, the coin and its icon — sending on the wrong network means losing the money, so on their screen all three are shown large.
admin.networks.readOnlyText: Opening and closing pairs, changing the icon and the minimum amount needs the "Fees, networks, companies" right.
admin.networks.iconHint: PNG, SVG or WebP. Square: the list crops it to a circle.
admin.networks.whereText: Every user now creates their own address, and it stays theirs: when money arrives the system knows whose payment it is and credits it without an operator. Issued addresses live under "Crypto addresses".
admin.networks.minDepositHint: Below this amount crediting goes to an operator: on a small transfer the network fee eats the whole thing.
admin.networks.sourceTitle: The list comes from the address service
admin.networks.sourceText: Networks and coins come from new.cryptocurrencyapi.net together with their icons: opening a network the service cannot issue an address on makes no sense. You can upload your own icon when the service does not provide one.
admin.addresses.title: Crypto addresses
admin.addresses.note: Addresses issued to users. An address belongs to one person — when money arrives on it the system knows whose payment it is and credits it without an operator.
admin.addresses.burnWarnText: The address will never be issued again. {name} will have to create a new one to top up. Past deposits stay in the history.
admin.addresses.emptyText: Nothing matches these filters. An address shows up here once a user creates it.
admin.operators.title: Operators
admin.operators.note: There is no public sign-up; operators are created by hand. Sign-in is email, password and TOTP; every action that moves money lands in the audit log.
admin.operators.noGrantText: Only a holder of GRANT_RIGHTS can grant rights. Initially that is the chief administrator.
admin.operators.name: Name
admin.operators.passwordHint: Issued once and changed by the operator on first sign-in. They set up the second factor themselves.
admin.operators.rightsHint: What is ticked is granted as soon as the operator is created.
admin.operators.oneByOneTitle: Grant them one at a time
admin.operators.oneByOneText: ADJUST_BALANCE creates money from thin air, WITHDRAW reduces a user’s balance. These two are granted deliberately, never «just in case».
admin.operators.newPasswordHint: Leave empty to keep the password. The current one cannot be shown: we do not store it in readable form.
admin.operators.superHint: The chief administrator’s rights cannot be removed: otherwise the system could end up with no holder of GRANT_RIGHTS at all.
admin.operators.resetHint: A reset is for when the operator has lost their phone. After it, sign-in requires setting the second factor up again.
admin.operators.resetWarnTitle: Until it is set up again, a password is the only protection
admin.operators.resetWarnText: Make sure it is this operator asking: the reset opens access to approving deposits and adjusting balances.
admin.operators.cantDeleteTitle: Cannot delete — there are audit log entries
admin.operators.cantDeleteText: Entries: {count}. The log is a financial record, and its entries must stay explicable. A disabled operator cannot sign in, but their past actions keep their author.
admin.operators.canDeleteText: The operator did nothing, so the record can be deleted. If in doubt, disable instead: that is reversible.
admin.depDrawer.title: Request from {name}
admin.depDrawer.creditedText: The entry is written, the user’s balance is increased by the net amount, the primary card limit is recomputed, and a notification is sent.
admin.depDrawer.rejectedText: The reason went to the user in full.
admin.depDrawer.readOnlyText: Approving and rejecting requests needs the APPROVE_DEPOSITS right.
admin.depDrawer.claimedText: Two people on one request means crediting it twice. If the operator has moved on, the request frees itself; until then the decision is theirs.
admin.depDrawer.amlSubtitle: The crediting threshold is {limit}. Above it the money is held.
admin.depDrawer.heldText: The check did not pass and the money was not credited. The only thing that can be done with it is sending it back to the sender.
admin.depDrawer.refundRequestedTitle: The user asked for a refund
admin.depDrawer.refundRequestedText: The user pressed refund in the app. The wallet service sends it and withholds the network fee.
admin.depDrawer.refundWaitText: The user starts the refund from the app: there is exactly one recipient — the sender address — so there is nothing to choose. The button below is for when the person does not answer and the money keeps sitting on the address.
admin.depDrawer.refundWarnTitle: The refund goes to the sender address
admin.depDrawer.refundWarnText: No other address can be entered: it is the only thing that identifies the sender. The money was never credited into the system — it sits on the crypto address and is not in the ledger.
admin.depDrawer.burnText: After the refund the address is no longer used and the user creates a new one. This one is already tied to that chain, and the next deposit would drag the same history along.
admin.depDrawer.refundSentText: The funds went back to the sender and the deposit address was burned.
admin.depDrawer.historySubtitle: Helps judge whether the amount is usual
admin.depDrawer.step1: A DEPOSIT entry in the ledger: gross, fee, net.
admin.depDrawer.step2: The user’s balance grows by the net amount.
admin.depDrawer.step3: The primary card limit is recomputed automatically.
admin.depDrawer.step4: If the user was in the red and is now positive, the cards unfreeze.
admin.depDrawer.step5: A notification to the user and an audit log entry.
admin.depDrawer.noCardsHint: If the user has no cards yet, the funds sit as an unallocated balance until the first card is issued.
admin.depDrawer.receivedHint: What arrived is what arrived. The declared amount is filled in as a hint and still needs confirming.
admin.depDrawer.overrideReasonPlaceholde: Required. It goes into the audit log.
admin.depDrawer.minText: A smaller amount can still be approved, but a reason is required.
admin.depDrawer.reasonHint: List items are translated by the dictionary. Free text is not: an English-speaking user would receive it in Russian.
admin.depDrawer.reasonBadge: The reason goes to the user in full
admin.userDrawer.blockedText: Sign-in is closed and the cards are frozen. This is reversible: unblocking restores access and unfreezes the cards that the block itself froze. The balance is untouched by a block.
admin.userDrawer.negativeText: All cards are frozen automatically. They unfreeze on their own once the balance reaches zero or above — no manual action needed.
admin.userDrawer.stuckTitle: Profile is stuck at the issuer
admin.userDrawer.stuckText: Their API has no cardholder-update routes. Only their account manager can resolve it.
admin.userDrawer.moneySubtitle: The ledger is the source of truth
admin.userDrawer.cardsSubtitle: Card details are never shown to an operator — there is no scenario for it
admin.userDrawer.canceledHint: Cancelled cards: {count}. They take no slot but are needed to make sense of the history.
admin.userDrawer.historySubtitle: Complete — that is what handling support requests needs
admin.userDrawer.feesSubtitle: A per-user rate REPLACES the global one, it is not added to it
admin.userDrawer.createInOxen: Create as a cardholder at Oxen
admin.userDrawer.reset2faNotice: The second factor and the recovery code have been reset
admin.userDrawer.reset2faWarnTitle: The old recovery code stops working
admin.userDrawer.reset2faWarnText: The user sets the second factor up again at their next sign-in and receives a new recovery code. The old one cannot be recovered.
admin.userDrawer.reset2faHint: Do this only once you are sure it is the account owner asking: resetting the second factor opens access to the cards and their details.
admin.userDrawer.withdrawNotice: Balance reduced. Hand the funds to the user.
admin.userDrawer.noTransferTitle: The system does not move money
admin.userDrawer.noTransferText: The balance drops and funds are released from the cards — the secondary ones first, the primary one last. The actual payout happens outside the system, by hand.
admin.userDrawer.adjustNotice: The adjustment is written to the audit log.
admin.userDrawer.adjustWarnTitle: The only operation that creates money from thin air
admin.userDrawer.adjustWarnText: It lands in the audit log with a loud marker.
admin.userDrawer.blockNotice: Status changed, the reason is written to the audit log.
admin.userDrawer.blockText: A block is reversible: sign-in is closed, all cards are frozen, and the user leaves the working lists. The balance is untouched — the money stays on the account until it is withdrawn by a separate action.
admin.userDrawer.blockReasonPlaceholder: Shown when unblocking, lands in the audit log
admin.userDrawer.offboardLead: This is not a separate status but a sequence of actions. The order matters:
admin.userDrawer.offboard1: Move all cards to closing — spending stops.
admin.userDrawer.offboard2: Wait for open authorizations to settle; the cards close themselves.
admin.userDrawer.offboard4: Process the withdrawal of the balance.
admin.userDrawer.offboard5: Block the user with a reason.
admin.userDrawer.offboardWarnTitle: The system warns if money is left on the account
admin.userDrawer.offboardWarnText: Blocking is still allowed — urgent cases happen.
